situation: A student who clearly studied did poorly and is convinced they are just bad at this subject.

dims.SPEAKABILITY: Card 2's lines are tighter and more natural — "I saw you working. That was real" and "Not whether you did it, I know you did" sound like actual speech, while Card 1's "A brain that studied and came up short is a brain that is still building the skill" is a mouthful no one would say aloud.
dims.SPECIFICITY: Both diagnose the same fixed-ability trap, but Card 2's status read — "being seen as someone who tried and still could not do it stings more than someone who simply did not bother" — cuts closer to why this student specifically retreats.
dims.TIGHTNESS: Card 2 carries less redundancy, whereas Card 1 repeats its "strategy not ceiling" point across nearly every section and pads the commitment line with meta-commentary about enjoying hardship.
dims.HONESTY: Card 2 names the harder truth more squarely — "effort without strategy change is not enough" — refusing the comfort that more of the same effort will fix it, while Card 1 leans slightly more on reassurance.
